rows.source: HSE biogas and anaerobic-digestion safety
rows.verified: Enclosed waste-processing buildings can accumulate biogas, including carbon dioxide and hydrogen sulphide, from biodegradation.

rows.source: HSE biogas and anaerobic-digestion safety
rows.verified: Mobile-plant and vehicle exhaust gases can add to atmosphere hazards in enclosed waste-processing areas.

rows.source: HSE biogas and anaerobic-digestion safety
rows.verified: Anaerobic digestion can recover energy from organic feedstocks and produce biomethane for the gas grid.

rows.source: HSE biogas and anaerobic-digestion safety
rows.verified: HSE enforcement records identify methane, hydrogen sulphide, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide and biological agents as relevant anaerobic-digestion hazards requiring assessment.

rows.source: HSE biogas and anaerobic-digestion safety
rows.verified: HSE enforcement records show that material plant changes require dangerous-substance and explosive-atmosphere risk assessments to be reviewed and updated.

rows.source: HSE biogas and anaerobic-digestion safety
rows.verified: Hydrogen sulphide can build up in poorly ventilated agricultural areas and is highly toxic.

rows.source: HSE biogas and anaerobic-digestion safety
rows.verified: Atmosphere testing, ventilation and emergency rescue arrangements are required before entering relevant confined spaces.

rows.source: HSE biogas and anaerobic-digestion safety
rows.verified: Waste-processing controls must account for bioaerosols as well as dangerous gas accumulation.

rows.source: HSE biogas and anaerobic-digestion safety
rows.verified: Biogas risk depends on feedstock, digestion stage, gas composition, plant integrity, ventilation, maintenance, ignition sources, confined spaces and emergency capability.

rows.source: HSE biogas and anaerobic-digestion safety
rows.verified: Biogas evidence is plant-, feedstock-, process-, atmosphere- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level explosion or poisoning probability.

rows.source: HSE hydrogen and CCUS major-hazard controls
rows.verified: Employers must protect workers and the public from risks arising from CCUS and offshore hydrogen-production activities.

rows.source: HSE hydrogen and CCUS major-hazard controls
rows.verified: From 6 April 2026, amended offshore requirements extend to CCUS installations, carbon-dioxide pipelines and offshore hydrogen production.

rows.source: HSE hydrogen and CCUS major-hazard controls
rows.verified: Operators and owners must prepare for fire, explosion and emergency response, including evacuation and recovery arrangements.

rows.source: HSE hydrogen and CCUS major-hazard controls
rows.verified: Relevant incidents involving CCUS wells or offshore hydrogen storage can be reportable under RIDDOR.

rows.source: HSE hydrogen and CCUS major-hazard controls
rows.verified: Hydrogen safety requires understanding its physical properties, phases and behaviour compared with traditional fuels.

rows.source: HSE hydrogen and CCUS major-hazard controls
rows.verified: Hydrogen-system design needs consideration of materials, gas detection, purging, handling and hazardous-area classification.

rows.source: HSE hydrogen and CCUS major-hazard controls
rows.verified: HSE research on liquid hydrogen supports development of accident-prevention and mitigation measures.

rows.source: HSE hydrogen and CCUS major-hazard controls
rows.verified: CCUS and offshore hydrogen dutyholders must comply with all health and safety legislation applicable to their activities.

rows.source: HSE hydrogen and CCUS major-hazard controls
rows.verified: Hydrogen and CCUS risk depends on phase, pressure, inventory, materials, containment, detection, ventilation, ignition, pipeline or offshore design and emergency response.

rows.source: HSE hydrogen and CCUS major-hazard controls
rows.verified: Hydrogen/CCUS evidence is technology-, installation-, phase-, route-, operating-condition- and scenario-specific and is not an exact parcel-level major-accident probability.
